title: Tool fanout result coalescer + idempotent retry semantics, OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments
author: Lena Thompson
description:
Motivation: Multi-tool call ergonomics have been a recurring source of edge cases in production: duplicated side-effects when retries occur, inconsistent result injection order when tools run in parallel, and poor streaming behavior for OpenAI-compatible clients when tool outputs are interleaved. This PR implements a small surface and runtime contract to make parallel tool execution idempotent-safe and to provide deterministic result coalescing while preserving streaming semantics for OpenAI-compat streaming endpoints.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a lightweight 'fanout coalescer' in the call_executor to collect tool outputs, canonicalize ordering, and attach deterministic metadata (call-id, attempt-id) so retries are recognized and dropped when duplicate. Introduces an idempotency key into the tool invocation layer; retries with same key now produce deduplicated results at the injector. Adjusts streaming adapter in the OpenAI compatibility layer so that streaming events for tool outputs are emitted as a consistent, monotonic sequence and include a new 'tool_chunk' envelope for downstream SDKs to reassemble. Updates SDK TypeScript helper to surface tool attempt metadata to application code and adds end-to-end integration tests.

Design notes: The coalescer maintains per-request transient state in memory (bounded map keyed by tool-call-id) and attaches an ordinal slot for each tool invocation based on the logical call graph generated during planning. When a tool returns, its output is buffered briefly (100ms by default) to allow aligned arrival of parallel calls; this avoids janky interleaving in the streaming API while keeping latency impact small for common workloads. The idempotency key is generated by the platform caller (or can be provided by the SDK) and is propagated through the public API headers. On receiving a retry, the coalescer checks (tool-call-id, idempotency-key, attempt-id) triple to determine uniqueness.

OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments: Previously, tool outputs interleaved raw tokens into the top-level event stream which caused downstream reassembly problems for clients expecting coherent 'tool' blocks. This patch adds a lightweight 'tool_chunk' event envelope: {"type":"tool_chunk","tool_id":"...","offset":123,"attempt_id":"...","data":"..."} so SDKs can accumulate chunks and publish a single 'tool_result' once coalesced. The server still emits partial results as streaming chunks but tags them explicitly to avoid confusion with assistant tokens. The compatibility adapter also upgrades connection-level metadata so that older SDKs still receive assistant tokens unchanged if they do not understand the 'tool_chunk' envelope (backwards compatible).

Developer ergonomics and API surface: - New header: X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency: <opaque-key> (optional). If omitted, the platform synthesizes one per request. - Tool call metadata available in streaming events and final result: attempt_id, idempotency_key, call_index. - Behavior guarantees: a single final tool_result will be injected per (tool-call-id, idempotency_key) pair, even with multiple attempts.

Testing and validation: Added integration tests that simulate parallel tool fanout with intentional delays and generated retries. Tests cover: deterministic ordering, deduplication on retries, streaming chunk reassembly, and fallback to legacy stream behavior for old clients. Load microbenchmarks show median end-to-end add-on latency of +8ms for typical 2-tool fanout and worst-case +43ms for bursty 8-tool scenarios (configurable buffer window reduced for latency-sensitive tenants).

Migration: No breaking changes. SDKs updated but older SDKs continue to work: they will receive chunked tool outputs as additional assistant tokens (compat path). We recommend SDK upgrades to take advantage of attempt metadata for safer side-effect handling.

Operational concerns: The coalescer uses an in-memory bounded cache with TTL; in Dedicated/Private deployments this stays node-local. For strict cross-node idempotency (rare), we added a toggle to persist minimal idempotency markers to the global metadata store (disabled by default). Metrics: new counters for tool_coalesce_count, tool_dedupe_count, tool_stream_chunk_bytes; new alert when tool_dedupe_rate > 5% over 5m.

Notes on rollout: Canary disabled by default in hosted; canary rollout plan added to Redwood Console: 10% traffic for 48h then 50% for 24h, monitor dedupe_count and latency.

Files changed and rationale (high level): server/tooling/call_executor.py - coalescer + idempotency checks; server/openai/compat/streaming_adapter.py - tool_chunk envelope and compatibility logic; sdk/ts/src/tooling.ts - helpers to reassemble tool chunks and expose attempt metadata; docs/api/tooling.md - updated API docs and header notes; tests/integration/test_tool_retries.py - new end-to-end scenarios; tests/unit/test_coalescer.py - unit coverage.

See commits for incremental steps and review comments below.

conversation: Aisha Patel (reviewer): Overall 👍. Two requests: make the coalescer buffer timeout config per-tenant and add a metric for coalescer-buffer-waits. Also please document the compatibility fallback clearly in docs.

Lena Thompson (author): Thanks — added per-tenant config with a sane default (100ms) and exposed tool_coalescer_buffer_waits metric. Updated docs to call out the fallback behavior and the header semantics.
Miguel Rivera (reviewer): Can you clarify behavior when a tool returns partial streaming then fails and is retried? Is the partial stream replayed or suppressed?

Lena Thompson (author): Partial streams are buffered and emitted as 'tool_chunk' pieces; on fail+retry we drop chunks from previous attempts that share the same (call-id, idempotency_key, attempt_id) triple. We retained a short tombstone window (500ms) to avoid race replays. Added unit test to cover this scenario.

Samir Gupta (reviewer): Unit tests look good. CI integration flaky: test_integration::test_tool_retries sometimes times out on macos-latest; re-run passed. Please monitor flaky test and file follow-up (ENG-4388).
Lena Thompson (author): Filed ENG-4388 for flaky CI, added increased timeout as a mitigation in this PR until the CI root cause is addressed.

Aisha Patel (approval): Approved after addressing metrics and docs.
Miguel Rivera (approval): Approved.
Samir Gupta (approval): Approved.
release_notes: User-visible: deterministic tool result ordering for parallel tool calls; idempotent retries prevent duplicate side-effects when SDK supplies X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency; streaming now emits explicit 'tool_chunk' events for easier reassembly. Operators: new metrics (tool_coalesce_count, tool_dedupe_count, tool_stream_chunk_bytes) and config for per-tenant coalescer buffer window.
